en.title: Harry Potter Director's Forgotten Sci-Fi Cartoon Surfaces 40 Years Later
en.summary: Before enchanting us with Hogwarts, **Chris Columbus** helmed a forgotten 1986 sci-fi cartoon. Now, as a new *Harry Potter* series looms, the director's early TV work is gaining a second look.
en.body:
Most fans know **Chris Columbus** as the visionary director who brought the magical world of **Harry Potter** to life on screen with 2001's *Sorcerer's Stone* and 2002's *Chamber of Secrets*. His name is now synonymous with the early cinematic adventures of the Boy Who Lived. However, long before Hogwarts students were casting spells, Columbus was already a rising star in Hollywood, having penned beloved scripts for *The Goonies* and *Gremlins*. Yet, his foray into television during this period produced a science-fiction cartoon that has largely faded from public memory: *My Secret Agent*.

Created in 1986, *My Secret Agent* was an animated series that explored the world of espionage and adventure, a far cry from the wizarding world that would later define Columbus's career. The show, which aired on CBS, featured a group of young secret agents tasked with global missions. While it showcased Columbus's early creative energies and his knack for crafting engaging narratives, it never achieved the lasting cultural impact of his film work. Today, the series is a curious footnote, a reminder that even celebrated directors have projects that don't quite stick the landing in the long run. It’s a stark contrast to the enduring legacy of the *Harry Potter* franchise, which is now gearing up for a comprehensive HBO reboot.

## A Look Back at Early Ambitions

Columbus's decision to return to television in the mid-80s, even after achieving film success, highlights the dynamic nature of the entertainment industry. While *My Secret Agent* may be forgotten, it represents a crucial period of growth for the director, allowing him to hone his storytelling skills in a different medium. This early work demonstrates a willingness to experiment with genres, a trait that would serve him well when tackling the immense challenge of adapting J.K. Rowling's complex magical universe. The animated series, though obscure, was part of a broader landscape of children's television that often blended adventure with important life lessons, a theme that would resonate even more powerfully in his later *Harry Potter* films.

## The Potter Legacy Continues

As the *Harry Potter* universe expands with a new television series in development, **Chris Columbus** has publicly voiced his support for the project. He believes the multi-season format offers a unique opportunity to delve deeper into the rich details of J.K. Rowling's books, aspects that were necessarily condensed in the films. "I think it's great that they're giving the books a chance to be told in a more faithful, detailed way," Columbus has said, emphasizing the potential for a more thorough exploration of the beloved saga. His endorsement suggests a positive outlook on the future of the franchise, even as he distances himself from direct involvement in the HBO reboot. The upcoming series, set to begin filming in summer 2025, promises a fresh take for a new generation of fans, while the older generation can look back at Columbus's journey, from forgotten cartoons to global blockbusters, with renewed appreciation.

## What's Next

While details surrounding the *My Secret Agent* series are scarce, the upcoming **Harry Potter** television series is slated to begin production in summer 2025, with casting and further creative announcements anticipated in the coming months. Fans eager to revisit Columbus's early work might find limited streaming options, but its existence serves as a fascinating reminder of his diverse career.

content_raw: In 1986, future Harry Potter director Chris Columbus had already found success with The Goonies and Gremlins, but he returned to TV to develop a sci-fi cartoon.
